title: Decision Rights in Human–AI Organizations: A Matched Simulation of Agent Autonomy, Human Accountability, and Review Workload
description: This working paper proposes a four-tier decision-rights model and evaluates its operational logic in a synthetic business-workflow sandbox using 1,000 matched cases across three governance configurations. Under default assumptions, the combined tiered policy and trusted mandate records 0 trials with unauthorized persistent mutations versus 268 and 5 in the alternatives, corresponding to 0, 376 and 7 changed database records, respectively. The combined arm routes 341 cases to review versus 785 under blanket review. The post-hoc ablation records 6 affected trials for tiers alone and 190 for the mandate alone. The results concern executable policy behavior under investigator-designed cases and oracle-based simulated reviewers, not live-model safety or workplace outcomes.
